headline: Bangladesh condemns drone attack targeting Makkah
summary: The government and political leaders express deep respect for the holy city and solidarity with Saudi Arabia after a drone was reportedly intercepted.
details: Saudi Arabia claims its air defense forces destroyed a drone targeting the holy city of Makkah before it entered restricted airspace. The incident prompted security alerts in Makkah, Jeddah, and Taif, though these were lifted shortly after.
The Bangladesh government has issued a strong condemnation of the attack. The Ministry of Foreign Affairs reaffirmed its deep respect for the dignity of Makkah and other holy sites in Saudi Arabia.
In a separate statement, Jamaat-e-Islami Amir Dr. Shafiqur Rahman also strongly condemned the attack, stating that any such attempt against the holiest place on Earth is completely unacceptable.
Saudi Arabia has described the drone attack attempt as a 'dark chapter.' This marks the first time since 2017 that such a security alert was issued for the holy city.
Yemen's Houthi rebels, who are often accused of such attacks, have denied the claims, calling the Saudi allegations 'completely false' in a statement to the Saba news agency.

In a separate statement, Jamaat-e-Islami Amir Dr. Shafiqur Rahman also strongly condemned the attack, stating that any such attempt against the holiest place on Earth is completely unacceptable.

Saudi Arabia has described the drone attack attempt as a 'dark chapter.' This marks the first time since 2017 that such a security alert was issued for the holy city.

headline_marked: Tk 2.5 lakh crore for metro: [[ECNEC approves new Metro Rail project]], revises two others
headline: Tk 2.5 lakh crore for metro: ECNEC approves new Metro Rail project, revises two others
summary: A new line from Gabtoli to Daserkandi will be built for Tk 45,503 crore, while costs for two existing projects were increased by over Tk 1.1 lakh crore.
details: The Executive Committee of the National Economic Council (ECNEC) has approved a new Metro Rail project connecting Gabtoli to Daserkandi, known as the Dhaka Mass Rapid Transit Development Project (Line-5) Southern Route.
The new project is estimated to cost Tk 45,503 crore. The decision was made during an ECNEC meeting chaired by Prime Minister Tarique Rahman at the Secretariat.
Additionally, ECNEC revised the costs of two other Metro Rail projects, increasing the total budget by Tk 1,10,443 crore. This marks the second time costs have been revised for these lines.
Following the revisions, the total cost for the MRT Line-5 Northern Route now stands at Tk 89,848 crore, and MRT Line-1 is estimated at Tk 1,14,394 crore.
Planning Minister of State Zunaid Abdur Rahim Saki explained that the projects were approved to avoid rising interest rates on JICA loans, which are expected to exceed 3% this month.
He noted that the costs increased because Bangladesh does not yet have the internal capacity to build metro rails independently, and Japan cannot construct them for less.
In total, ECNEC approved 12 projects worth Tk 1,68,780 crore, including seven new and five revised projects.

Other approved projects include district highway development in Rajshahi and Chattogram, electrification of the Narayanganj-Dhaka-Joydebpur rail route, and a new dual-gauge railway from Bogura to Sirajganj.
